title: Victoria Falls, Hwange and the Matobo Hills
best_months: May to October (dry season: game concentrates on Hwange's pumped waterholes and walking is at its best). Avoid planning the A8 drive in December to March if you can: the rains make a damaged road worse, and a 4×4 is recommended in Hwange in those months.
summary: Two nights at the Falls, five in Hwange split between a treehouse lodge near the main road and a camp on the park's eastern boundary, one night in Bulawayo, three among the granite domes of the Matobo Hills. The long day is Hwange to Bulawayo on the A8, a road under slow repair, which is why the plan breaks it with a night in town rather than pushing through. Matobo is the counterweight to Hwange: fewer animals, more rock art, and rhino tracked on foot.
vehicle: High-clearance 4×4 or large SUV (e.g. a double-cab 4×4 pickup), not a sedan. The A8 between Victoria Falls and Bulawayo is badly potholed along much of its length; at least one major rental firm describes it as unsuitable for sedans, recommends high-clearance vehicles and forbids night driving on it. A 4×4 is specifically needed for the 32 km of dirt into The Hide and for Hwange's gravel roads in the rains. Matobo is tar from Bulawayo to Maleme Dam; most park gravel roads suit any vehicle in the dry, but Whovi Game Park and some outlying areas need high clearance or 4×4. No camping kit needed.
start: Victoria Falls (Victoria Falls International Airport, VFA)
end: Bulawayo (Joshua Mqabuko Nkomo International Airport, BUQ, with nonstop flights to Johannesburg), or loop back to Victoria Falls with an overnight in Hwange

days.notes: Collect the vehicle at the airport. Two nights: the Rainforest walk at the Falls (ZimParks entry US$58 incl. VAT for international adults in 2026, per secondary reports), the 1pm vulture feeding at Victoria Falls Safari Lodge, a sunset on the upper Zambezi. Stock up on USD small notes and groceries in town; fuel up before leaving.

days.to: Ivory Lodge, Sikumi Forest (eastern edge of Hwange, near Dete)
days.distance_km: approx. 175–180 (Ivory Lodge sits about 2.5–3 km off the A8)
days.drive_hours: 2.5–4.5 (sources disagree; the A8 has potholed and slow stretches)
days.road_surface: Tar (A8, potholed in places, rehabilitation in progress); last 2.5–3 km dirt, 4×4 recommended
days.notes: Leave mid-morning so the drive is done well before dark; night driving on the A8 is not advised (and is forbidden by at least one rental company). Lunch option: Hwange Safari Lodge, which is open to non-residents for food and drink, just before the Main Camp gate. The Painted Dog Conservation visitor centre at Dete (opposite Hwange airport) is a short detour; hours and fee unverified, email ahead. Ivory's rate includes park fees and two activities a day, so game drives into Hwange go in the lodge's vehicle.

days.to: The Hide, eastern boundary of Hwange National Park
days.distance_km: approx. 25–30 to Main Camp, then about 32 to camp (unverified total)
days.drive_hours: 1.5–2 (The Hide says a little over an hour from Main Camp)
days.road_surface: Tar to Main Camp (23 km tar from the Cross Mabale turn-off); about 32 km of dirt from Main Camp to camp, 4×4 required
days.notes: Enter Hwange at Main Camp and pay fees at reception. Get directions from The Hide in advance (they supply them on request). If you'd rather not drive the dirt, The Hide runs a transfer from Main Camp (free for stays of three nights or more, per its 2025 published fees). Three nights qualifies for Dove's Nest, the treehouse sleep-out, subject to availability. Davison's alternative: park at Ngweshla picnic site inside Main Camp (24-hour security) by 13:00 and transfer in by the camp's vehicle.

days.distance_km: approx. 340 (about 32 to Main Camp, 23 to Cross Mabale, 283 Cross Mabale to Bulawayo)
days.drive_hours: 6–8 (unverified; estimate scaled from one rental firm's 8–9 hours for the full 440 km Falls–Bulawayo road)
days.road_surface: Dirt to Main Camp, then tar; the A8 east of Hwange has had some of the worst reported sections (Halfway–Gwayi, Lupane–Cross Jotsholo, Insuza–Lupane in older reports)
days.notes: The long day. Leave after breakfast, not after the morning drive. Halfway House is a small service station on the A8 about 230 km from Bulawayo; whether it currently sells fuel and food is unverified, so fuel up at Hwange town or Dete side before setting off. Arrive in Bulawayo before dark. Stock up at a Bulawayo supermarket for Matobo.

days.road_surface: Tar: Robert Mugabe Way becomes Matopos Road, two-lane tar to the park boundary (about 30 km), then single-lane tar towards Maleme Dam
days.notes: Three nights: rhino tracking on foot with a licensed guide, San rock art in the caves, World's View (Malindidzimu) and Rhodes' grave. Self-drivers can explore the park's gravel roads in the dry; leave Whovi Game Park and the remoter tracks to a guided drive unless you're in a 4×4.

days.to: Bulawayo airport (BUQ), or back towards Victoria Falls
days.distance_km: approx. 45–60 to BUQ; approx. 485 back to Victoria Falls
days.drive_hours: About 1 to the airport; the return to the Falls should be split with a night in Hwange
days.notes: Ending in Bulawayo needs a one-way rental (Falls pick-up, Bulawayo drop), which at least one rental firm discourages on this road; confirm availability and fee with our partners in Victoria Falls before quoting. The loop back to the Falls adds two days (one night in Hwange, e.g. Ivory Lodge or Hwange Safari Lodge) and keeps a same-location return.

stays.name: Victoria Falls Safari Lodge
stays.area: Victoria Falls town, on the edge of Zambezi National Park
stays.access_notes: In Victoria Falls town, tar access (unverified detail). Rate includes a complimentary shuttle to town and the Rainforest.
stays.rate_basis: Bed and breakfast, per person sharing, Lodge Standard Room, green season 1 Jan–30 Jun (US$330 1 Jul–31 Dec); waterhole-facing rooms from US$330
stays.sets_it_apart: A daily 1pm vulture feeding (Vulture Culture) in front of the lodge, free to watch, with donations going to the Victoria Falls Wildlife Trust; rooms face a waterhole.
guided_activities: Falls and river activities bookable through the lodge (unverified list)
stays.ownership: Part of the Victoria Falls Safari Collection (operator name per its rates page; parent company unverified)
stays.why_we_list_it: Hundreds of vultures come down to the lawn at one o'clock, and the lodge has fed them for years in support of the local wildlife trust. Some rooms look onto a waterhole, and a shuttle runs to the Falls. It is the right price for a first night after a long flight.
stays.cautions: Bed and breakfast only; dinner and activities extra. Vulture numbers have fallen in some years (2020 report). Large lodge, not a camp.

stays.name: Ilala Lodge Hotel
stays.access_notes: Town-centre hotel; road surface and parking unverified.
stays.rate_basis: Bed and breakfast, per person sharing, Classic Room (third-party listings: Chalo Africa, Siyabona)
stays.sets_it_apart: Walking distance to the Falls (unverified; to confirm with property).
stays.why_we_list_it: Draft pending verification: a town hotel close enough to the Rainforest to walk, for travellers who want the Falls at first light without a transfer.
stays.cautions: Facts beyond the rate are unverified; needs a proper property check before it can go in the collection. Hotel, not a safari lodge; no guided wildlife activities of its own confirmed.

stays.name: The Elephant Camp
stays.area: Private concession near Batoka Gorge, Victoria Falls
stays.access_notes: About 15 minutes from town; free self-parking at the property per booking sites. Access road surface unverified. Two scheduled shuttles a day into town.
stays.rate_basis: Fully inclusive, per person sharing, 11 Jan–31 Mar 2026 (US$1,042 Apr–May; Go2Africa lists US$877 Jun–Oct, Safari.com US$1,087). A sustainability and conservation levy applies (US$50 pppn on the 2027 rate page; 2026 levy unverified).
stays.sets_it_apart: View over Batoka Gorge to the Falls spray; the Wild Star Sleepout bush platform; tie to the Victoria Falls Wildlife Trust.
stays.why_we_list_it: The splurge at the start of the trip. The gorge drops away below the camp and the Falls spray hangs on the horizon, and one night can be spent on an open platform in the bush. It sits well above our usual price band, and we say so.
stays.cautions: Above the US$150–600 band; include only as the clearly-labelled higher option. Rates vary between sellers; confirm with Wild Horizons.

stays.name: Ivory Lodge
stays.area: Sikumi Forest, private concession on the eastern edge of Hwange National Park
stays.access_notes: About 2.5–3 km off the Victoria Falls–Bulawayo road; a 4×4 is recommended for the last few kilometres of dirt. 173–180 km from Victoria Falls, 258–263 km from Bulawayo, 24–30 km to Main Camp gate (sources vary). Contact lodge to confirm current road conditions.
stays.rate_basis: Fully inclusive, per person sharing, Treehouse, Jan–Apr and Nov–Dec (US$568 May–Oct); includes meals, local drinks, two activities a day and national park fees
stays.sets_it_apart: Seven thatched treehouses and a floodlit hide a short walk from the lodge, overlooking a waterhole; an elevated star bed reached by night drive.
stays.ownership: Amalinda Collection (owner-run group that also owns Amalinda Lodge in Matobo), per Yellow Zebra Safaris
stays.why_we_list_it: The lodge is a few minutes off the main road but the treehouses face a waterhole, and the hide below them is lit after dark. Park fees and guided drives are in the rate, so the first Hwange days need no planning. It also links naturally with Amalinda in Matobo, under the same owners.
stays.cautions: Room counts differ between sources (nine units in all). Conservation levy and Painted Dog entry excluded. Proximity to the A8 means some road and railway noise is possible (unverified).

stays.name: Hwange Safari Lodge
stays.area: Private concession outside Hwange National Park, about 12 km from Main Camp
stays.access_notes: Self-drive on tar. Open to non-residents for food and drink; suggested as a brunch stop before the Main Camp gate.
stays.rate_basis: Full board, per person sharing, low season (Victoria Falls Guide listing; secondary)
stays.sets_it_apart: A big lodge with a waterhole in front of it, on tar, ten minutes from the park gate: a reliable lunch stop and fallback bed.
stays.why_we_list_it: Not a destination. It is where the tar ends and the park begins: lunch on the terrace looking at a waterhole, fuel for the afternoon, and a dependable bed if a plan changes.
stays.cautions: Large (around 100 rooms, about 200 guests); does not pass the friend test as a main stay. Listed as on the road only.

stays.name: The Hide
stays.area: Private concession on the eastern boundary of Hwange National Park
stays.access_notes: The camp states guests may self-drive into camp in their own 4WD vehicles; directions on request. About 32 km of dirt from Main Camp, a little over an hour's drive. Alternative: transfer from Main Camp (US$50 pp return for stays of two nights or fewer; free for three nights or more, per 2025 published fees).
stays.rate_basis: Fully inclusive, per person sharing, low season (Victoria Falls Guide listing; The Hide's own rate card is a PDF not yet read). Seasons: green 1 Nov–31 Mar, mid 1 Apr–31 May, high 1 Jun–31 Oct.
stays.sets_it_apart: The waterhole hide the camp is named for; up to four activities a day including walks and night drives; Dove's Nest treehouse sleep-out free on stays of three nights or more; children of any age at Tom's Little Hide.
stays.why_we_list_it: A family-run camp of ten tents looking onto one waterhole, with a hide beside it. Stay three nights and one of them can be spent in the treehouse. It is one of the few camps in this part of Hwange you can drive yourself to, provided the vehicle is a 4×4.
stays.cautions: 4×4 essential for self-drive; arrive in daylight. Rate is from a secondary source; get the rack rate PDF. Coordinates from the camp's own access page.

stays.name: Davison's Camp
stays.area: Linkwasha-Makalolo concession, south-eastern Hwange National Park
stays.access_notes: Drive to Main Camp, sign in and pay park fees, then park at Ngweshla picnic site 280 m past the boom (24-hour security). The camp's game-drive vehicle collects you for the roughly one-hour transfer, 56 km on the main park dirt road. Arrive by 13:00 and coordinate with the camp's Victoria Falls office. Self-drivers cannot drive into private concessions.
stays.rate_basis: Per person sharing, shoulder 1 Nov–19 Dec 2026 (Wilderness listing on Safari.com); US$720 green season Apr–May and US$1,010 peak Jun–Oct 2026
stays.sets_it_apart: Named for Ted Davison, Hwange's first warden; walking on a private concession; elephant-monitoring activities.
stays.why_we_list_it: The handover is the point: you leave the car under guard at Ngweshla and the camp's guide takes over for the deep south-east of the park, where self-drivers aren't allowed. Nine tents, a walking guide, and the same concession as Wilderness's dearer camps.
stays.cautions: Above the band in peak season (US$1,010). Car is parked inside the park for the length of the stay; confirm insurance cover with the rental company.

stays.name: Camelthorn Lodge
stays.area: Ngamo, private concession on the south-eastern boundary of Hwange
stays.access_notes: Most guests drive to Halfway House, a small service station on the A8, and meet their guide there for a drive of a couple of hours to camp. Whether self-drivers can leave a vehicle securely at Halfway House is unverified; confirm with Imvelo. Ten minutes from the lodge's private gate into the park.
stays.rate_basis: Fully inclusive, per person sharing, all year (Victoria Falls Guide listing; secondary)
stays.sets_it_apart: A sunken hide at the waterhole; pump runs to the waterholes Imvelo maintains in southern Hwange; rhino on the community side.
stays.why_we_list_it: Halfway House is on the way to Bulawayo, so this is the Hwange camp that fits the route east. Guests ride out on the pump run that keeps southern Hwange's waterholes filled, and the sunken hide puts you at ground level beside the waterhole.
stays.cautions: Self-drive parking arrangement unverified; do not sell as park-and-transfer until Imvelo confirms. One review describes 'a very bumpy 50 km' on the way in.

stays.name: The Bulawayo Club
stays.access_notes: City centre; free parking listed by the owner.
stays.rate_basis: Room rate incl. breakfast; booking-site snapshots ranged about US$89–100 per room for two in early 2026 (Expedia, Travelocity). Per-person figure not published; indicative only.
stays.sets_it_apart: A historic members' club building in the city centre, with a library and garden, and fifteen en-suite rooms.
stays.why_we_list_it: After a day on the A8, a room in an old gentlemen's club with a library and a garden. It is well under our usual price, and that is the point of a night on the road.
stays.cautions: Founding date and history not yet sourced; don't publish historical claims until checked. Rates from booking sites only.

stays.name: Travellers' Guest House
stays.sets_it_apart: Garden with a pool and bougainvillea; family rooms. Close to the Zonkizizwe shopping centre (two supermarkets, fenced and guarded car park) for stocking up before Matobo.
stays.why_we_list_it: A garden guest house in the suburbs, for families and anyone who would rather not drive into the city centre at the end of the A8.
stays.cautions: Single first-hand source (a 2026 travel journal of an August 2024 stay). Needs rates and a property check before publishing.

stays.name: Amalinda Lodge
stays.area: Matobo Hills, about 45 km south of Bulawayo on the Matopos road
stays.access_notes: Self-drive access listed as yes (Tracks4Africa). Tar from Bulawayo along Matopos Road; approx. one hour from Bulawayo airport.
stays.rate_basis: Fully inclusive, per person sharing, Nov–Dec 2026 (Go2Africa); US$447 April 2026, US$570–613 May–Oct 2026 depending on seller
stays.sets_it_apart: Suites built into granite boulders; rhino tracking on foot and by vehicle; San rock art in nearby caves.
guided_activities: Rhino tracking (on foot and by vehicle)
stays.ownership: Owner-run; the first lodge in the Amalinda Collection (formerly Camp Amalinda)
stays.why_we_list_it: The rooms are built into the granite, some of them against the rock itself. The guides take you out on foot after white and black rhino, then to caves with San rock paintings. It is the reason to drive past Bulawayo.
stays.cautions: Peak-season rate near the top of the band. Room count not stated consistently (nine en-suite per one source).

stays.name: Big Cave Camp
stays.area: Private wilderness area about 3 km from the Matobo National Park entrance, 49 km south of Bulawayo
stays.access_notes: Self-drive via Bulawayo on the Matopos road; about an hour from Bulawayo airport. Final access road surface unverified.
stays.rate_basis: International, per person sharing, 5 Jan–31 Mar (US$400 1 Apr–31 Oct); meal basis unclear (another listing on the same site says fully inclusive). B&B, half and full board plans offered.
stays.sets_it_apart: Ten thatched A-frame chalets on a granite whaleback, with a lounge built round a boulder and trees growing through the roof; natural rock pool.
guided_activities: Rhino tracking in the national park (ZimParks-licensed guides)
Game drives and guided walks on the property
stays.why_we_list_it: Owner-run, ten chalets on a whaleback of granite, with the bar built round a boulder and trees coming up through the thatch. Rhino tracking in the park goes out with licensed guides, at a lower price than Amalinda.
stays.cautions: Meal basis of the 2026 rate to confirm. A third-party listing says US dollars cash only (possibly outdated). Child conservancy levy US$15 per child per night (ages 6–17) on the camp's booking page.

stays.name: Farmhouse Lodge
stays.area: Granite Ridge Wildlife Reserve, bordering Matobo National Park, 48 km south of Bulawayo
stays.access_notes: Self-drive via Bulawayo on the Matopos road into Granite Ridge Wildlife Reserve; about an hour from Bulawayo airport.
stays.rate_basis: International, per person sharing, all year (US$140 single). Basis listed as half board on the Matobo accommodation index; activities paid separately.
stays.sets_it_apart: Twelve Cape Dutch-style cottages with kitchenettes on a private reserve with a resident guide; rhino tracked on foot; a viewing platform over a water point.
guided_activities: Rhino tracking in the national park
stays.why_we_list_it: Owner-run cottages with their own kitchens on a reserve that borders the park, and a full-time guide who walks guests out to rhino. The least expensive bed on the route that still comes with a guide, and a good one for families.
stays.cautions: Below the usual band; activities extra. Owner identity and current guide licensing to confirm.

borders: No land border on the core route: arrive and depart by air at Victoria Falls (VFA) and/or Bulawayo (BUQ).
If joined to R3 (Four Corners), the Kazungula (Botswana) and Victoria Falls Bridge (Zambia) crossings apply; requirements to be researched with R3 (unverified here).
practicalities.fuel: Most fuel retailers transact in US dollars (NewsDay survey, April 2026), with supply described as adequate by government in March 2026. Fill up in Victoria Falls and Bulawayo; Hwange town and Dete are the main towns between. Fuel inside Hwange National Park is not confirmed by any source. Halfway House on the A8 is a small service station but current fuel availability is unverified. Card acceptance at pumps unverified: carry USD cash.
practicalities.cash_and_payments: Most transactions are in USD; the ZiG local currency is in limited circulation and cash shortages can occur (Swedish embassy guidance, June 2026). Bring enough USD cash, in small notes, for fuel, park fees, tips and fines. Some smaller lodges may be cash only (Big Cave, per a dated third-party listing).
practicalities.park_fees: Hwange: international overnight visitor US$12 per day (Great Zimbabwe Guide, June 2026; not confirmed against the official tariff). Foreign-registered vehicle US$10 day visitor / US$3 accommodated visitor for Hwange and Matobo (secondary source citing the 2026 ZimParks tariff). Matobo per-person fee: unverified (secondary sources conflict, US$15–20). Victoria Falls Rainforest: US$58 incl. VAT for international adults in 2026 (news reports). Paid at Main Camp, Sinamatella or Robins reception, or through the lodge. Ivory Lodge includes park fees in its rate. Official 2026 tariff: https://www.zimparks.org.zw/media/2026/02/De-Gazetted-Tariff-2026.pdf (not yet read: file too large to fetch).
practicalities.gate_times: Hwange: 06:00–18:00 per secondary listings (Main Camp campsite listing, Robins Camp guide); self-drive in daylight only; no self-drive between Main Camp and Sinamatella after 14:00, or Main Camp and Robins after 12:00; ZimParks accommodation check-in by 17:30. Matobo: 06:00–18:00 per one secondary source (unverified). Confirm with ZimParks.
practicalities.roadblocks_and_police: Expect police roadblocks. Warning triangles are the item most consistently linked to recent fines on tourists (February 2026 reports; US$30 fines). Also carry a fire extinguisher (an SAZ-approved, secured one has been specified in past guidance), a reflective vest, and keep vehicle papers and licence to hand. Police leadership instructed officers in January 2025 to prioritise major offences over minor infractions; enforcement remains inconsistent. Ask for an official receipt for any fine. Rental vehicles should come with the required kit: confirm at handover.
practicalities.rental_and_cross_border: Rental desks operate in the Victoria Falls airport terminal. For this route, book a high-clearance 4×4 or large SUV: Europcar Zimbabwe's advisory says the A8 has 'deteriorated considerably', is unsuitable for sedans, can take 8–9 hours end to end at 20–30 km/h in places, and forbids night driving on it. The same advisory discourages one-way drops between Bulawayo and Victoria Falls, so ending in Bulawayo needs a confirmed one-way arrangement and fee. Cross-border permission not needed for R1 alone. Per house rules, user-facing copy names no rental company; 'our partners in Victoria Falls' until D-03 is settled. An international driving permit is advised (secondary source).

variants: Loop back to the Falls (12–13 nights): Matobo → Hwange (one night at Ivory Lodge or Hwange Safari Lodge) → Victoria Falls, avoiding a one-way rental.
Imvelo version of Hwange: swap The Hide for Camelthorn Lodge and meet the guide at Halfway House on the A8, which sits on the way to Bulawayo (subject to Imvelo confirming secure parking).
Hand over the keys: park at Ngweshla and spend the deep-Hwange nights at Davison's Camp with Wilderness guiding.
Short version (8–9 nights): Falls 2, Hwange 3 (one camp), Bulawayo 1, Matobo 2.
Falls, both ways: join R3 (Chobe and the Zambezi Region) before or after this route from Victoria Falls.
